profile.reading:
The Terminal Annex is a large historic post office building at 900 North Alameda Street in downtown Los Angeles, next to Union Station and the city's Chinatown and Civic Center districts. Built between 1938 and 1940, it is recognized as a California Historical Landmark and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its architecture and its role in the city's mail handling history during the mid twentieth century, when Los Angeles grew into one of the country's major postal hubs.

The building is owned and operated by the United States Postal Service, an independent federal agency, and its primary documented function remains postal. Mail processing and related USPS operations tied to its historic role as a rail adjacent terminal facility are what the public record actually describes. Some equipment and engineering references associated with the building point to IT and network infrastructure being housed within it alongside its postal functions, which would be consistent with USPS's general practice of folding data and network equipment into its existing nationwide real estate footprint rather than building purpose made data center campuses for every regional need. That practice does not make the Terminal Annex primarily a data center, however, and no USPS publication, capacity disclosure, or independent source describes this site as a dedicated data center facility with its own power, cooling, or tenancy profile. Its public identity, landmark status, and available documentation all center on its postal and historic architectural significance rather than any computing infrastructure it may also contain.

reading.body:
The Terminal Annex in downtown Los Angeles is a historic post office building built in 1938-1940 and listed as a California Historical Landmark, operated by the United States Postal Service as a postal facility. Engineering documentation indicates IT infrastructure is housed within the building alongside mail processing operations, consistent with USPS practice of maintaining regional data and network systems in existing real estate rather than building dedicated data centers. The facility's published capacity is not disclosed.

No independent source describes the Terminal Annex as a purpose-built data center, and USPS has published no specification of its IT load, cooling capacity, or power draw. Without published megawatt figures, the site cannot be ranked against other California facilities or assessed for its contribution to regional AI infrastructure scaling. California has 103 mapped data center sites and 11 with published capacity totaling 365 MW.

The Terminal Annex is not usable as a data point for tracking the grid constraint on AI scaling. It may house USPS network infrastructure, but that is distinct from the commercial hyperscaler and specialized AI compute campuses this site tracks. Its primary documented identity and public obligation are postal operations and historic preservation, not data center operations.
